notes: UC Santa Cruz students have the option to complete one or more minors, provided they complete all of the required coursework for the minor(s). The sponsoring department establishes the course requirements for a minor. The minor involves substantial work in the discipline and requires no fewer than 25 upper-division or graduate credits. The minor appears on the student's official transcript but not on the diploma. Students do not apply for admission into a minor when applying to UC Santa Cruz. If interested in completing a minor, transfer students must contact the department sponsoring the minor after enrolling at UCSC.

Please visit the department's website to learn more about this minor: https://jewishstudies.ucsc.edu/index.html PREPARATION FOR THE MINOR One of the following core courses: HIS 74: Introduction to Jewish History and Cultures HIS 74A: Introduction to Middle Eastern and North African Jewish History: Ancient to Early Modern HIS 74B: Introduction to Middle Eastern and North African Jewish History, 1500-2000 HIS 75: Film and the Holocaust HIS 76: The Holocaust: A Global Perspective LIT 61J: Introduction to Jewish Literature and Culture Plus up to two lower-division courses, from the core courses above or the following electives: HIS 2A: The World to 1500 HIS 2B: The World Since 1500 HIS 70A: Modern European History, 1500-1815 HIS 70B: Modern European History, 1815-present HIS 78: Modern Authoritarianism in Europe and Beyond MUSC 80I: Music of Modern Israel MUSC 80T: Mizrach: Jewish Music in the Lands of Islam MUSC 80Y: Music, Anti-Semitism, and the Holocaust MUSC 81P: History of Jewish Music
